To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) trellis-shape coding can recover almost all shaping loss and (b) PIP can recover 1-2 dB of the power and modulo losses.
trellis shaping recovers shaping loss and that partial interference presubstraction (PIP) recovers power loss.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and performance evaluation of trellis and block convolutional codes that are combined with Tomlinson Harashima precoding for the presubstraction of multiuser interference at the transmitter.
the design of a trellis and/or convolution code that can be used with THP to achieve a target data rate.
the design of trellis-shape codes for the presubtracted interference channel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
trellis shaping and PIP can recover almost all of precoding losses, and that a combination of the schemes can be used to achieve near-capacity performance in a multiuser interference channel.
the combination of trellis shaping with PIP recovers almost all precoding loss at rates of 3, 2, and 1 bits per transmission.
trellis shaping and PIP can together be used to recover all of the losses of THP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
trellis and PIP schemes can be applied to convolutional codes to recover the precoding losses, but that the gains are not as large as for trellis codes.
the proposed trellis-shape-PIP scheme is able to reduce the loss of the conventional THP to less than 0.5 dB.

, with a combination of trellis shaping, PIP, and convolutional precoders, it is possible to achieve the same error performance as a conventional system that does not have the advantage of transmitter-side interference presubtraction but that has a higher SNR by about 1-1 1/2 dB.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of trellis and/or convolutional codes with THP is able to recover most of the losses incurred by the application of practical codes.
the combination of trellis shaping and PIP is a promising technique for practical interference presubtraction in the presence of channel coding.
, in the presence of a noncausally known interference signal, it is possible to recover most of the precoding losses.
